People always ask me when they should visit Edinburgh. Well, it depends on what you want. In August, we have the festival, and the city is wonderful, but it's very crowded, and hotels are expensive. Winter is magical, especially at New Year, but it gets dark at four in the afternoon, and when the weather is bad, some places close early. So if you come in the winter, bring warm clothes and check the opening hours. My favorite season? The spring. The days are longer, the parks are green, and the streets are calm. I've lived here all my life, and I still think April is the best month of the year.

I've traveled to more than forty countries, and people think every trip was perfect. It wasn't. A few years ago, I went to Iceland in the winter. I had a plan for every day. On the second day, a storm closed all the roads, and I spent two days in a small hotel. At first I was angry. Then I started to talk to the other guests. A couple from Japan, a family from Brazil, two students from Canada. We cooked together and shared travel stories until midnight. I never saw the waterfalls on my list. But that trip is the one I remember the most. Sometimes the trip that goes wrong is the best story.

For years I traveled in the high season, like everybody else. Europe in July, Peru in the dry season. And every time, it was the same story: crowded streets, expensive hotels, and hours in lines. So I changed. Now I travel in the off-season. The weather isn't perfect, sure. But hotels and flights are much cheaper, and I can actually talk to the locals, because they're not too busy. My one rule is this: the places with a limited number of visitors, like a famous museum or a castle, I always book in advance. Everything else, I decide on the day.
